newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bakrie group to control Inovax after deal.
newsitem.headline: Bakrie group to control Inovax after deal.

text.p: Drug maker and distributor Inovax Ltd said on Monday that a consortium led by Indonesia's Bakrie Group was expected to have majority control of the company once an acquisition was completed later this calendar year.
Inovax managing director Tony Fitzgerald said Bakrie and other investors would help finance the company's A$94.6 million purchase of Indonesian drug maker PT Ponco, announced earlier on Monday.
The investment group would outlay about A$60.8 million in new equity in Inovax, which Fitzgerald said would represent about 66 million shares out of a total of 126 million shares on issue.
The Bakrie Group is a privately-held company which controls Bakrie and Brothers.
Fitzgerald told Reuters that Ponco and its holding company Circa International had been acquired from the Saputra family, with the acquisition due for completion in September 1997.
He said the purchase prices consisted of cash, vendor finance and the assumption of about A$20 million of liabilities.
Ponco was founded in 1971 and was expected to hae sales of A$38 million in 1997.
